runs.name: American Electric Power Company, Inc.; NYSE AEP, SEC CIK 0000004904, New York, 10-K filer; one of the largest investor-owned electric public utility holding companies in the United States, generation, transmission and distribution to more than five million retail customers in eleven states, four segments (Vertically Integrated Utilities, Transmission and Distribution Utilities, AEP Transmission Holdco, Generation & Marketing); no rename, merger, spin-off or split in the 8-Ks since December 2025; a 19.9% stake in Midwest Transmission Holdings sold June 2025 for about $2.78B net; the 10-K names no SEC-filing rival, Duke, Dominion and FirstEnergy chosen as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: Price **$127.14** (close 2026-10-16, printed by `tools/run.py` from an aggregator, flagged). Shares 544,397,352 at 2026-07-30 from the 10-Q cover (0000004904-26-000059), checked against 545,549,444 issued less 1,186,815 treasury; the six further cover lines are the subsidiary co-registrants, not added; about 45M shares under forward sale agreements not counted. Sovereign **5.43%**, the US Treasury 30-year par yield of 2026-10-16 (issuing authority). Read from the 10-K for 2025 (0000004904-26-000013), the Q2 2026 10-Q, the 2026 proxy (0000004904-26-000022), the 10-Ks for 2024, 2022, 2019 and 2016, the 8-Ks, and the SEC order of 2025-01-17 (Release No. 11356, File No. 3-22425, found by web search and fetched from sec.gov); 2025 operating cash $6,944M checked to the filed statement. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, stated in the run file. `tools/run.py`'s capital-spending column found wrong for this filer (acquisitions of generation facilities in place of construction expenditures); owner cash rebuilt from the filed cash-flow statements. **Q1 IN**: a regulated return on capital put in, authorized returns 9.25% to 10.50% on equity. **Q2 IN**: an exclusive legal franchise, its regulated return carried to Q3 as the regulated exception; Vertically Integrated Utilities deciding at 43.7% of five-year segment earnings; comparators Duke, Dominion and FirstEnergy, mean return on book equity 2016 to 2025 10.0% for AEP against 6.7%, 9.7% and -0.6%. **Q3 weighs against**: owner cash after all spending negative in nine of ten years 2016 to 2025; growth funded by debt, shares issued every year and the minority sale; added capital about 8% pre-tax. **Q4 weighs against, no STOP**: specified items removed from featured operating earnings every year, guidance set and beaten, the $19M SEC penalty removed from operating earnings, the SEC's finding that the 2019 10-K omitted related-party payments; carried to Q5. **Q5 OUT on integrity**: the SEC order (settled without admitting or denying) found AEP formed, funded and controlled Empowering Ohio's Economy, which paid $1.2M to groups tied to the Ohio Speaker later sentenced for racketeering, and found the 2020-07-27 press release misleading, an $850M equity-unit offering announced 15 days later; the FY2024 10-K, four weeks after the order, kept 'does not believe that AEP was involved in any wrongful conduct'; four 2020 directors remain, including the Lead Director; doubt closes the file by **[M2013-088]**; ability weighs for. **COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE**: owner cash 2021 to 2025 with depreciation as maintenance $3,461M a year all-equity ($2,091M after interest), $(2,670)M after all spending; net debt $52,316M at 2026-06-30 plus a $2.8B minority claim (a CONVENTION of the run); value range **$15.81 to $28.20 a share all-equity** (equity-only $75.24 to $116.31); expected return 2.8% to 5.1% at the price, no case earns the floor, the price above the top of every range; fair price $(46.90) all-equity, $37.73 equity-only. Debt $22.0B (2016) to $48.8B (2025) and $52.8B at 2026-06-30, debt to equity 1.26 to 1.65; interest covered 2.84 times in 2025. Contamination declared by the analyst: AEE commit subjects, a `Test Runs/` listing of thirteen other 2026-10-18 run names (none opened, none about AEP), memory-index queue lines; none used. Commits 8e79be36 (template), 72fc5f84 (Step 0, Q1), a7d43490 (Q2), 894462da (Q3), 29f0339d (Q4), 4cfd5a50 (Q5), 1d956148 (Q6 to Q12 not reached, Q7 computation, the box), bac1379c (self-audit, notes). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` 65 ids no problem; the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` no E-id, no missing id, 51 adjacent quoted fragments, **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) no rule for integrity when the misconduct was under a former chief executive but part of the board and the company's response continue; (2) the all-equity ten percent floor cannot be met by a utility allowed about ten percent on book equity; (3) the statutory-tax recomputation at a cost-of-service utility, where tax savings pass to customers (the analyst confessed a convention not to apply it); (4) the serial-acquirer test when owner cash before purchases is negative; (5) specific (e) does not say at what level to carry growth spending for ten years (window average $4.76B used against the plan's about $14.4B); (6) `tools/run.py` should prefer the construction-expenditure tag. Not armed: the box is not OUT at Q7 or IN. Could not get: a maintenance-capex figure, the 10-Q's finance-lease figure, peer figures read in their filed statements.
runs.narr: OUT at Q5 on integrity (American Electric Power Company, NYSE AEP; regulated electric utilities in eleven states and transmission; Q1 IN; Q2 IN as the regulated exception, Vertically Integrated Utilities deciding at 43.7%; Q3 against, owner cash after all spending negative nine of ten years; Q4 no STOP, against, the SEC penalty removed from operating earnings; Q5 OUT on the SEC order of 2025-01-17 on Empowering Ohio's Economy and the July 2020 release, the post-order 10-K denial and the 2020 directors remaining; COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value range $15.81 to $28.20 all-equity at $127.14, no case earns the floor, fair $(46.90) all-equity, $37.73 equity-only; no citation slip; not held; not armed; framework gaps for the operator: integrity across a change of chief executive, the all-equity floor at a utility, Whose tax at a cost-of-service utility, (e)'s growth-spending level, tools/run.py's capital-spending tag)
